summary.headline: Jindal Saw Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA fell to INR413 crore and PAT to INR114 crore, with export shipments suspended since March 2026 due to MENA conflict.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 weakened versus Q3 on both standalone and consolidated bases, missing management's prior guidance that Q4 would beat Q3. Standalone EBITDA was INR413 crore (Q3: INR527 crore) and PAT was INR114 crore (Q3: INR227 crore), while FY26 standalone EBITDA fell 47% and PAT fell 58% year on year. Management attributed the drop to weak ductile iron pipe demand from slow Jal Jeevan Mission execution, suspended exports from March 1, 2026 after MENA force majeure, a INR48 crore forex loss, and an API monogram suspension on seamless pipes. Net debt declined, with standalone net debt at INR2,453 crore. Management guided that Q1 FY27 will also be affected.

segments.name: Ductile iron pipes (domestic water)
segments.commentary: Main source of weakness amid slow Jal Jeevan Mission execution; management sees oversupply in DI capacity. Q4 water sales said to be slightly above Q3, mostly state-funded orders routed via EPCs.

segments.name: Export and MENA business
segments.commentary: No exports shipped since March 1, 2026 under force majeure; about 30,000-40,000 tonnes ready for shipment deferred. Export order book includes a 6 lakh tonne job-work order from Saudi Arabia, with about 2 lakh tonnes of steel supplied by the buyer held in stock. MENA accounts for roughly 29-30% of order book.

segments.name: Carbon seamless / API pipes
segments.commentary: API monogram use suspended after a February 2026 API audit found nonconformances. NCs closed; API auditors revisit the Nashik factory in May 2026, but no approval timeline was given. Production is being shifted to other seamless products.

segments.name: Abu Dhabi subsidiary
segments.commentary: Delivered about 48,000 tonnes in Q4 FY26 versus 52,000 tonnes in Q3. Order book about $180 million, or about 171,000 tonnes, equal to roughly 9 months of operations. Sales limited to customers within trucking range.

segments.name: Jindal Hunting JV (51%)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR149 crore and PAT INR43.2 crore in FY26, versus INR177 crore revenue and INR51.5 crore PAT in FY25.

segments.name: Stainless steel pipes (welded and seamless)
segments.commentary: Management is moving toward higher-end, approval-gated grades for margin. Rajeev Goyal said the business as a whole faces margin pressure, with any upgrade benefit expected in H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 expected to remain affected by the MENA logistics disruption and weak domestic water demand; a few more weeks or months of impact flagged.
Management says it can ramp up quickly once shipping normalises, and will push deferred export shipments immediately; the deferred revenue is expected to be recognised in FY27.
Capex guidance: INR500-600 crore in FY27 across Indian sites, then INR400-500 crore in FY28, mainly debottlenecking and replacement, with no major new Indian greenfield or brownfield plant.
Management expects the Jal Jeevan Mission momentum to pick up, with execution possibly starting post-monsoon; the timing was described as uncertain.
Management declined to say whether margins have bottomed, citing freight, crude and inflation uncertainty.
capex_capacity: Abu Dhabi seamless carbon pipe plant (subsidiary, 100% owned): land with fuel infrastructure secured, equipment ordering and LCs under way, long-term land lease signed with AD Ports; debt-equity and project cost still being revised.
Saudi Arabia LSAW and HSAW facility via a JV (Jindal 51%, Buhur Group 49%): land secured for one project, LC opened for some equipment.
Management says Abu Dhabi and Saudi projects will be fast-tracked; Saudi's net balance-sheet impact is lower given the 51% stake.
Capex spent in FY25-26 was about INR800 crore; roughly 10 Indian locations, with recent spending mostly on debottlenecking, efficiency and staff infrastructure.
Management says India's DI capacity is in oversupply and it will work with existing capacity, with options such as product mix shifts and export and domestic shifts for ductile lines.
demand_pricing: Water (DI) demand deferred, not lost, per management. Work is now mostly state-funded orders via EPCs, which are priced differently from older Jal Jeevan orders.

Management expects new pipeline demand from MENA energy-security shifts, India's gas pipeline fast-track order (March 2026), and ONGC deepwater projects of about $20 billion. Domestic seamless demand is about 1.5 million tonnes per management.
Steel is bought only against firm orders, so raw-material swings fall on the manufacturer; most international sales are on a delivered basis, so freight and diesel costs hit margins.
Ductile pricing has a pig-iron-linked escalation clause, covering roughly 30-35% of contracts and mainly the domestic market; some states also have escalation clauses.

Competition is rising in Saudi, with local factories being set up by rivals. Management expects imports to continue to serve most Saudi demand for about a year, and says its own plants are fully booked for a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is there DI overcapacity, and will utilisation and margins recover quickly?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Goyal said DI pipes have oversupply, while longitudinal, helical and seamless capacity is adequate for demand. DI utilisation will stay low until Jal Jeevan Mission gets going.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue was lost to the Middle East disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a deferment, not a loss. About 30,000-40,000 tonnes were ready for shipment; the value is above INR30-40 crore, according to management.

qa_highlights.question: Is the seamless and stainless steel margin going to improve, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects seamless margins to improve as demand stays robust, and stainless steel to benefit from upper-end approvals, with impact in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new order intake strategy in helical SAW, and does the industry have capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is fully booked for a couple of quarters and will not take immediate low-margin domestic orders. It says the export order book will return once shipping normalises.

qa_highlights.question: What peak debt and net debt/EBITDA are acceptable during capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said standalone long-term debt is about INR525 crore and consolidated about INR650 crore, and the balance sheet can take more debt. It said debt/EBITDA including working capital could reach 2-2.5x if EBITDA returns to about INR3,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is there pass-through on coal or raw-material costs, and how is DI execution progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the escalation pass-through is mainly pig-iron linked and domestic, with coal stocks held and shipped quarterly. DI execution is shifting to state-backed orders, and Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 execution is expected to take a month or two to start.

risks_watch: MENA shipping and force majeure: export shipments suspended since March 1, 2026 with no reopening date; about 30,000-40,000 tonnes deferred.
API monogram approval for seamless pipes: auditor revisit in May 2026, with no timeline given.
DI oversupply and slow Jal Jeevan Mission and EPC payment liquidity; execution may not resume until post-monsoon.
Rupee depreciation (88.88 to 94.84 per dollar) and forex revaluation hits; INR48 crore loss in Q4.
Rising freight and crude/diesel costs on delivered contracts; pass-through limited.
Debt rising from the Abu Dhabi and Saudi capex; Delhi High Court NTPC litigation pending, with the order reserved after 1-2 more hearings.

summary.management_tone: Management was candid about weakness, acknowledging Q4 missed its own guidance and that the outlook is unpredictable, but stayed confident on medium-term recovery in MENA and in liquidity and balance sheet strength. It was evasive on margin bottoming, coal pass-through, Jal Jeevan timing and API approval timing, citing uncertainty and declining to give timelines.

growth.why: Management guided no revenue growth number; Q4 standalone income fell ~7% QoQ and FY26 standalone EBITDA fell 47% YoY, with Q1 FY27 expected to remain affected by MENA export suspension and weak domestic DI demand, partly offset by an order book (Abu Dhabi ~$180m, ~9 months) and deferred export revenue expected in FY27, but no new Indian capacity is planned and DI capacity is in oversupply.
